name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. '_4d' is the dispatch-table index 0x4D (entry @ 0x51CC5), a domain ID, not an address residue. Descriptor corrected from '__unref_sentinel' to '__ch29_dragon_down_2': the slot is LIVE, reached via the ch29 kill-drop path -- ch29 char_spawn_record[1] = a defense-core dragon (enemy_data 59, char_id 0x7F, lv30) carries pickup_kind=2 param=0x4D, so the dragon's death dispatches consequence[0x4D], setting tile_event_consumed_flags[0x13]=1 to mark this dragon destroyed (one of the ch29 3-dragon objective flags 0x12/0x13/0x14 set by 0x49/0x4D/0x4E). The earlier 'unref' verdict only scanned turn-event/tile-step hooks and missed the kill-drop path; the 'priming handler_47' framing was a cross-chapter artifact (0x47 is ch28) -- here flag[0x13] is a ch29 dragon marker.
purpose: Chapter 29 defense-core-dragon progress marker (dispatch slot 0x4D, reached via the ch29 kill-drop path when the dragon record[1] enemy_data 59, pickup_kind=2 param=0x4D, falls): marks this dragon destroyed by setting tile_event_consumed_flags[0x13] = 1 (one of the 3-dragon objective flags), with no other side effects.
logic_summary: Loads the tile-event consumed-flags base pointer (data_fd2_field_map_tile_event_consumed_flags_ptr @ 0x53AD5) and stores 1 into byte [base+0x13]. No other side effects, no branches, ignores its arg. Disasm: PUSH 4; CALL __CHK (Watcom stack probe); MOV EAX,[0x53AD5]; MOV byte [EAX+0x13],1; RET. Self-contained 10-byte stub, no borrowed tail. In ch29 this flag[0x13] is one of the 3-dragon objective progress markers (0x12/0x13/0x14 set by 0x49/0x4D/0x4E); the consumed-flags array is per-battle, so the ch28 handler_47 relationship does not apply here.
